sorries.obstruction: an inextensible causal curve of A ∩ B is in general extensible in A and in B; that it meets φ(Σ) needs (1) every causal curve of A (resp. B) over an interval to lie on an inextensible one of A (CurvesExtend relative to an open set, Zorn-type), (2) the two extensions to leave A ∩ B through one end point, which must exist in A and in B (a limit along the curve) and be unique (Hausdorff), and (3) at an end point in A ∩ B a short causal curve inside A ∩ B (J^±_{A∩B}(p) ≠ {p} with local causal arc-connectedness). None is proved for topological spacetimes, and the paper gives no argument. The three facts are neither proved nor carried as hypotheses, so the abstract statement of exists_mem_image_inf MAY BE FALSE in the setting of topological spacetimes: its truth there is unestablished, and c_ext_connexe rests on it. The sorry-free core is c_ext_connexe_of_isCauchySurfaceOn, which takes the paper's unargued step 'φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B' (l.1940-1941) as a named hypothesis.

findings: ETT.tex:1940-1941: 'The map M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding, so φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B' is asserted without argument. That φ(Σ) meets each causal curve of A∩B at most once is proved (eq_of_mem_image_inter); that it meets every inextensible curve of A∩B is the open step. In the Lorentzian case it holds by an end-point argument (the future end points of the two extensions coincide and would lie in (A∖B) ∩ (B∖A)).

ETT.tex:1941-1942: 'every point of A∩B lies on an inextensible causal curve' — the existence of inextensible causal curves through every point is proved nowhere (GerochEquiv's SCOPE notes the same gap); carried as a model fact.

sorries.obstruction: Two points of the step '(∧, φ) ∈ ℰ' are not argued in the paper: (1) condition (b) of ℰ does not ask φ_M injective and nothing shows the glued φ injective, so ∧ → M₂ is not shown to be a Cauchy embedding (WP-4; a gap in the argument, not a refutation — injectivity is plausibly recoverable); (2) the inclusion of i₁(M₀) into the union ∧ = ⋃M is not shown to be a Cauchy embedding: neither global hyperbolicity of ∧ nor that i₁(Σ₀) meets every inextensible curve of ∧ follows from the same facts for each M. Two further obstructions belong to the ABSTRACTION, not to the paper's proof: (3) the library's causality has no gluing axiom (kb/0014), so the strong-morphism condition of φ on ∧ does not follow from its restrictions; (4) maximality and uniqueness need (b(N), c∘b⁻¹) ∈ ℰ, i.e. b(N) with the causality restricted from M₁ globally hyperbolic with a Cauchy surface, which a local isomorphism of non-local causalities does not transport without absolute minimality. The gluing step also uses lem:C_ext_connexe, itself resting on the sorry exists_mem_image_inf.

findings: ETT.tex:1953-1960 (confirms WP-4): ℰ's condition (b) does not ask φ_M injective, so the step '(∧, φ) ∈ ℰ, hence ∧ is a common sub-extension' does not show ∧ → M₂ injective. A gap in the argument, not a refutation: no counterexample is known, and injectivity is plausibly recoverable.

ETT.tex:1960-1961: 'Thus (∧, φ) ∈ ℰ' needs that the inclusion of i₁(M₀) into the union ∧ is a Cauchy embedding (global hyperbolicity of ∧ and the Cauchy property of i₁(Σ₀) in ∧), which does not follow from the same facts for each M; it is not argued.

hypotheses.note: IsMinimal quantifies only over over-extensions whose carrier is in Type u (the universe of M₀, M₁, M₂); unlike sub-extensions, over-extensions are not bounded in size by M₁ or M₂, so this restricts the quantifier. self_isMinimal's hypothesis (the two embeddings of every over-extension coincide) is not witnessed

questions: Minimality asks for a morphism M → M' to every common over-extension M', not a unique one. Is uniqueness intended (a universal property)? Under rigidity the map out of the gluing is unique (exists_unique_desc).

kb_proposals: The component of an inextensible curve c over I in an open set U is inextensible in U: Causality.inextensible_ordConnectedComponent with mathlib's ordConnectedComponent (I ∩ c⁻¹' U) t₀; needs M causal and Hausdorff; the past end is the future end of C.dual (dual_futureInextensible_iff).

Splicing a future extension of a final segment J ⊆ I into one of the whole curve: Causality.futureExtensible_of_final (shift by δ = φ t₀ − t₀, CurveOn.concat, comp_affine with k := 1 and all implicits named); the new value is new for all of c only because M is causal.

A Cauchy surface (DEC-14) is acausal only under CurvesExtend (every causal curve over a segment lies on an inextensible one, a named model fact) and causal arc-connectedness: Causality.IsCauchySurface.isAcausal. Arguments 'a causal curve meeting Σ twice' about finite curves need it.

Abstract E≥0-morphisms on an open set W: IsEMorphismOn (= StrongMorphism ∧ LocalIsomorphism on W = ⊤, isEMorphism_iff). Curves, inextensibility and Cauchy surfaces transport between V ⊆ W and φ(V) (isCauchySurfaceOn_image_iff); get Nonempty M from a curve point, then use invFunOn and InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn.
Rigidity (rem:CBG_analytique) does not follow from 'local homeomorphism + morphism of topological spacetimes': timelikeLine_not_isRigid (kinkIso). Carry IsRigid as a named hypothesis.

`[[a, b]]` needs `open scoped Interval`; a structure declared under `variable (...) in` only takes the variables it mentions (CommonOverExtension has no C₀ argument); a def named `trivial` in a namespace shadows `trivial` in every declaration of that namespace.
